A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same UDora research, with matching authors, methods, benchmarks, and appendix case studies. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of the text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices without material reading gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original attack-success experiments on three benchmarks, ablations in Tables 4–5 and Figure 3, and real-agent attack demonstrations in Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and demonstrations, with the real-agent appendix renamed B, and adds measured computational timings in Section 5.

M1.justification: Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the scoring function, insertion modes, string optimization, and iterative procedure. The surrogate-response clarification, altered diagram formulas, and suggested efficiency shortcuts do not establish a revision to the implemented method.

E1.justification: Both evaluate InjecAgent, WebShop, and AgentHarm with the same attack scenarios and retain the Perplexity and AutoGen demonstrations. Autonomous driving is newly discussed only as related work.

E2.justification: Tables 1–3 retain identical comparator membership: GCG and Prompt Injection on InjecAgent/WebShop, and GCG and Template Attack on AgentHarm, alongside No Attack. Newly cited defenses are not evaluated as comparators.

E3.justification: Section 5 adds evaluation of mean per-iteration time, separating response collection from string optimization. Existing sample counts, filtering, model versions, optimization budgets, and ASR criteria remain unchanged. Suggested ten-step updates and 100-token responses are not documented as settings used for the benchmark results.

E4.justification: The attack-efficiency analysis expands from iteration counts to a computational-cost breakdown across two models and two datasets. Existing insertion-location and optimization-mode ablations, Figure 3, and appendix case studies remain unchanged; proposed defenses receive no experimental analysis.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, uncertainty bars, or significance tests. The added timing averages do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Section 5 newly reports query/optimization times in seconds: Llama 3.1 gives 3.48/11.22 on AgentHarm and 5.57/5.97 on InjecAgent; Ministral gives 2.49/6.04 and 6.86/8.18, respectively. All numerical entries in Tables 1–5 and the retained benchmark and appendix outcomes are unchanged.

T1.justification: Figure 2 changes the sequential objective from one positional score to a sum over n positions, and changes the joint sum's upper limit from n to l. This is a limited mathematical specification revision. Equation (1) and the body formulation remain unchanged, including n+1 sequential positions, leaving the diagram's notation imperfectly reconciled.

C1.justification: Both claim a unified attack covering malicious environments and instructions, optimization using agents' own reasoning, superior ASR across three benchmarks, and successful real-agent attacks. The revised abstract and contribution wording retain this scientific scope.

C2.justification: v2 adds a tentative hallucination interpretation of the WebShop examples and identifies string optimization as the runtime bottleneck. Section 7 adds potential defenses involving restricted reasoning access, guardrails, adversarial training, and detection, with utility tradeoffs and detection difficulties. Existing limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract adds a code-repository access pointer, and Section 5 discloses computational timings and possible efficiency shortcuts. Existing hyperparameters and the appendix's GPT-4o log-probability optimization details are retained. Repository contents or availability cannot be verified from the PDFs.

R1.justification: v2 adds references to A Language Agent for Autonomous Driving, ChatScene, GuardAgent, AGrail, and KnowHalu. These provide limited extensions concerning driving applications, defenses, and hallucination; the central positioning against existing attack methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 rewrites the abstract, reorganizes the introductory procedure into numbered steps, and clarifies surrogate-response terminology. It adds discussion subheadings, removes the empty Experiment Details appendix heading, renumbers appendices B/C to A/B, and updates publication and contact text. Most prose and the overall narrative structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 2's optimization formulas are revised, Algorithm 1 and several tables are relocated, and Figure 3 moves between columns. Running titles are removed and a publication footer is added. The same five tables and eleven figures remain, with appendix illustrations preserved.

improvement.justification: v2 clarifies that modified reasoning supplies a surrogate optimization objective, adds a code-access pointer and runtime breakdown, and discusses defense tradeoffs. These improve clarity and practical transparency. Gains remain limited because benchmark evidence is unchanged, defenses are untested, and Figure 2 retains a notation inconsistency with Section 3.
